title: Ketamine
sources: Pamplin J, Fisher AD, Penny A, et al. Analgesia and Sedation Management During Prolonged Field Care. Joint Trauma System CPG ID: 61. 1 April 2017
Remley M, Loos P, Riesberg J, et al. Prolonged Casualty Care Guidelines. Joint Trauma System CPG ID: 91. 21 Dec 2021, rapid update June 2023

changelog.change: Added the prolonged sedation infusion (JTS PCC protocol): loading dose, starting rate, mix concentration, titration step, and the one-drug-per-bag / RASS-monitoring cautions.
Imported from AnesCalc v2 DrugCard.swift via tools/import-anescalc.mjs.

mechanism: Non-competitive NMDA receptor antagonist → dissociative anesthesia. Also activates σ, opioid, and muscarinic receptors. Sympathomimetic via indirect catecholamine release. Bronchodilator via β-adrenergic pathway.
onset: IV ~30 sec; IM 3–4 min; IN 5–10 min
dosing:
Induction (IV): 1–2 mg/kg
Induction (IM): 4–6 mg/kg
TIVA adjunct infusion: 0.1–0.5 mg/kg/hr
Sub-dissociative analgesia bolus: 0.1–0.5 mg/kg IV
Sub-dissociative infusion (OIH-sparing): 0.15 mg/kg/hr
Pediatric intranasal: 3–5 mg/kg
Prolonged sedation infusion (mechanically ventilated / prolonged casualty care, JTS CPG 61): load 1 mg/kg IV/IO over 60 sec, then start 1.5 mg/kg/hr (25 mcg/kg/min). Mix 750 mg in 250 mL NS (3 mg/mL) — dial-flow rate at the starting dose ≈ weight (kg) ÷ 2, in mL/hr. Titrate ±0.25 mg/kg/hr at a time, reassessing before each step.
cautions: AEs: Hypertension, tachycardia, emergence reactions/hallucinations (~12%), ↑ICP, ↑IOP, ↑secretions, nystagmus; laryngeal reflexes preserved but NOT protective
CI: Conditions where ↑BP is hazardous — uncontrolled severe HTN, acute CAD (relative); hypersensitivity

Precautions: Pair with glycopyrrolate to reduce secretions; midazolam or dark quiet room reduces emergence reactions; OIH with prolonged high-dose infusion; pediatric neurotoxicity; GU complications with chronic use

On a prolonged sedation infusion: run ketamine alone — don't mix a second drug into the same bag (the in-solution interaction isn't well studied). If sedation stays inadequate on ketamine alone, get a critical-care consult before starting a second infusion; use opioid or midazolam PUSH doses, not a second drip, to smooth peaks and troughs. Respiratory depression becomes more likely above 1 mg/kg given quickly by fast IV/IO push.
pearls: Drug of choice for hemodynamically unstable induction (trauma, sepsis, hypovolemia). Bronchodilator — preferred in reactive airway disease.
NMDA antagonism reduces opioid consumption and may prevent OIH. Laryngeal reflexes maintained but NOT protective — aspiration risk persists.

On an infusion, reassess sedation depth on a clinical scale (e.g. RASS) at regular intervals rather than relying on vitals alone; add capnography to standard monitoring (BP cuff, pulse oximeter, auscultation) if available.
